issues.description: Control frame stores a live FrameProcessor reference instead of a stable identifier.
issues.detail: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame.service holds a FrameProcessor instance. Control frames should carry value-like identity (name or id), not live runtime handles. The current shape breaks serialization, retains swapped-out services via GC, and couples the frame to mutable runtime state. Pass a service_name or id and resolve at the switcher.

issues.description: Equality check on FrameProcessor relies on default __eq__ and is fragile.
issues.detail: `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` works only because FrameProcessor inherits identity equality. A future __eq__ override, wrapper, or proxy silently changes routing and leaks the frame downstream. Use `is` for explicit identity comparison, or compare a stable id, and document the invariant.

issues.description: Forward-reference annotation "FrameProcessor" is unresolved in frames.py.
issues.detail: The dataclass field annotation is a string and works at runtime only because dataclasses don't resolve annotations. Any get_type_hints call, pydantic adapter, or schema introspection will fail unless FrameProcessor is importable. Add a TYPE_CHECKING import or weaken the annotation to Any with a documented contract.

issues.description: Suppression invariant in push_frame is implicit and undocumented.
issues.detail: The new branch only drops the frame when it targets the active service, assuming no inactive-service request frames ever reach push_frame. That holds today because the dispatcher only sends to the active service, but the invariant is implicit. Add a literate comment explaining the chain, or assert it defensively.

issues.description: STTService now forwards the request frame downstream, leaking it outside a switcher.
issues.detail: Old code suppressed RequestMetadataFrame at the STT boundary; new code pushes it downstream relying on ServiceSwitcher to swallow it. When STTService is used standalone without a switcher, the frame escapes into the rest of the pipeline. Document the contract or consume the frame when no switcher is present.

synthesis.summary: The rename and targeting refinement is structurally sound, but the panel converges on one shape problem: embedding a live FrameProcessor reference inside a control frame and comparing it with `==` is the wrong data structure. Control frames should carry identifiers (name or id), not live processor handles, and identity checks should be explicit. Secondary concerns include an unresolved forward-reference annotation, an implicit suppression invariant in push_frame, and STTService now leaking the request frame downstream when used outside a switcher. NEEDS-WORK: fix the service-field shape and identity comparison, then the patch lands cleanly.
